title: CELPIP Listening: Six Parts, One Play
summary: The CELPIP Listening parts, the fact that audio plays only once, and the note-taking habit that saves your score.

nodes.label: Plays once
nodes.note: No replays — listen the first time

nodes.label: Questions after
nodes.note: You answer once the audio ends

chunks.heading: You hear it once — so listen actively
chunks.body: Each audio passage **plays only once**, and the **questions appear after** the audio ends. There are **no replays**, so you must **listen actively the first time** and take notes as you go. Missing the first listen means guessing.
chunks.realExample: Because questions come after the audio, you can't read them while listening — so jot key facts (names, numbers, the problem, the decision) as you hear them, ready for whatever's asked.
chunks.memoryHook: One play, questions after. Note the key facts live — there's no rewind.

chunks.heading: Everyday and workplace situations
chunks.body: The parts move through **real-life Canadian contexts** — a problem-solving conversation, a daily-life chat, an information segment, a news item, a discussion, and viewpoints. Listen for **purpose, key details, and the speaker's attitude**, not every word.
chunks.realExample: In a problem-solving conversation, catch what the problem is and what each speaker suggests — those decisions are what the questions ask about.
chunks.memoryHook: Catch purpose + key detail + attitude. Situations are everyday, not academic.

chunks.heading: Note-taking is the whole skill
chunks.body: Use the **scratch paper** to capture **names, numbers, dates and the outcome** as you listen. Your notes — not your memory — answer the detail questions, especially in longer segments like the news item or discussion.
chunks.realExample: For a news item, note who/what/where/when and any figure mentioned; a question will almost certainly hinge on one of those specifics.
chunks.memoryHook: Who / what / number / outcome — write it down. Notes beat memory.

chunks.heading: Don't stall on one question
chunks.body: Since there's **no penalty for wrong answers**, never leave a blank, and don't freeze on a question you missed — **make your best choice and keep pace** so you're ready for the next audio. Some items are unscored trial questions, so a tough one may not even count.
chunks.realExample: Missed a detail? Pick the most likely option and move on — dwelling on it risks missing the start of the next passage, which you also can't replay.
chunks.memoryHook: Best guess, keep moving. No penalty, and some items don't even count.

recall.q: How many times does each CELPIP listening audio play, and when do questions appear?
recall.a: Each audio plays only once, and the questions appear after the audio ends.

recall.q: Why is note-taking essential in CELPIP Listening?
recall.a: There are no replays, so your notes of names, numbers, dates and outcomes — not memory — answer the detail questions.

recall.q: What should you listen for rather than trying to catch every word?
recall.a: The purpose, key details and the speaker's attitude.

recall.q: Should you leave a listening question blank if unsure?
recall.a: No — there's no penalty for wrong answers, so always make your best choice.

recall.q: What kinds of situations does CELPIP Listening cover?
recall.a: Everyday and workplace Canadian contexts — problem-solving, daily-life conversation, information, a news item, a discussion and viewpoints.
